questions.title: Which company will hold the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign firm as of July 10, 2026?
questions.background: Alibaba's 2014 US initial public offering raised $25 billion, setting the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign company.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official issuer announcements and contemporaneous reporting by reputable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the company reported as holding the all-time record for the largest US initial public offering by a foreign company as of July 10, 2026. Compare offerings by proceeds raised, not company valuation. An offering whose pricing and share sales have been announced may qualify before exchange trading begins. Accepted Answer Format : The company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 1 reporting (Korea Times, Yonhap, Aju Press) confirms SK hynix completed its amended Form F-1/A filing with the SEC on June 30 (US time), cleanly incorporating the June 25 Northern District of California DRAM antitrust class action into Risk Factors without delaying its schedule. Crucially, Korea Times reports an earlier, tighter calendar than previously cited: bookbuilding starts July 6, final pricing is set for July 9 (a full day ahead of the July 10 cutoff, and pricing qualifies under resolution criteria), and Nasdaq trading begins July 10. Macro and sector tailwinds also strengthened sharply on July 1: South Korea's June exports surpassed $100B for the first time ($102.25B, +70.9% YoY) led by a +199.5% YoY surge in semiconductors ($44.8B), SK hynix rose +0.26% in Seoul trading, and oil hit a 4-month low as US-Iran Doha talks eased war risk. At ~$29.4B-$29.47B (17.79M shares), the offering sits ~18% above Alibaba's $25B record before any greenshoe. Lifting SK Hynix from 0.69 to 0.77 while keeping 0.23 on Alibaba for tight holiday-week SEC effectiveness risk (July 3 US holiday), blank offering terms prior to bookbuilding, extreme KOSPI volatility/ADR discount risk, and minor definitional risk.

questions.current_reasoning: Sharp July 1 repricing across liquid prediction markets ($23M+ Kalshi, $4.7M Polymarket) and NBA free-agency moves narrows the race into a virtual dead heat between Golden State and Cleveland. Conversely, the Cleveland Cavaliers surged from 0.15 to 0.35 (jumping to 34-38% on Kalshi, 33% on Polymarket, and -150 favorite on BetOnline, partly fueled by viral hometown-reunion buzz we discount slightly alongside ESPN's Ben Golliver citing an East executive calling Cleveland 'the cleanest fit' after their ECF run). The Miami Heat drop from 0.25 to 0.18 (18% Kalshi, 21% Polymarket, 5/1 BetOnline) after spending $6.5M of their NTMLE on Tim Hardaway Jr. and facing Giannis Antetokounmpo stylistic-fit questions. The San Antonio Spurs are eliminated from our top five (0.04 -> <0.01) after Marc Stein reported they are not pursuing James and San Antonio spent their NTMLE on Tobias Harris (2yr/$31M). On Klutch's 'Game Over' podcast July 1, Rich Paul said he spoke with 12-14 teams and market size won't matter if James can contend; confirmed July 1 outreach brings in the Denver Nuggets (0.035, Denver Post/Marc Stein, BetOnline cut 50/1 -> 25/1) and Minnesota Timberwolves (0.025, The Athletic, 2-3% Kalshi/Polymarket, 18/1 BetOnline), leaving 5.0% for the rest of the league (Knicks, Wizards, Thunder, etc.) ahead of the July 6 moratorium lift.

Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the purchasing ownership group in the first sale of the Seattle Seahawks formally approved by NFL owners during 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the purchasing group or the family leading it.
questions.current_reasoning: June 29 Seattle Times coverage citing Bloomberg News reports that first-round bids to buy the Seattle Seahawks were due Monday, June 29 (earlier than previously rumored July 6), that no new potential buyers have emerged beyond the three previously identified groups (Aditya Mittal & Wyc Grousbeck, Todd Boehly, and Vinod Khosla), and that the bidder pool is 'fairly shallow' and 'shrinking' as the record $9B-$10B valuation tests billionaires' cash appetite. Confirming a shallow pool with no newly reported suitors on bid-deadline day concentrates probability mass onto the three active groups (Mittal/Grousbeck 0.30, Boehly 0.25, Khosla 0.23; combined 0.78, up from 0.66), while trimming unmentioned names Apostolopoulos (0.04), Bezos (0.03), and the unannounced mystery-bidder tail (from 23% to 15%).

questions.title: Which major US employment sector will shed the most jobs in July 2026?
questions.background: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports monthly changes in nonfarm payroll employment by sector.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the broad employment sector with the largest net decline in payroll jobs in July 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' initial employment report for that month, released in August 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-07 Accepted Answer Format : Compare sectors by the number of jobs lost, not percentage changes, and count subsectors within their parent sectors. Answer with the sector's name.
questions.current_reasoning: In the BLS May 2026 report, Financial activities was the largest broad-sector decliner (-22,000, down 107,000 over 12 months, after -11,000 in April), while Information led declines in April (-13,000, -2,000 in May, 16 straight months of tech losses). Because the question counts subsectors within broad BLS parent sectors by total jobs lost, large sluggish sectors with high monthly variance—Professional and business services (+6k May, +7k Apr), Manufacturing (+7k May with nondurables -10k, -2k Apr), and Trade, transportation, and utilities (-2.8k net in May)—also carry substantial probability. Roughly 23% remains outside the top five (chiefly Government due to July education seasonal swings, Leisure and hospitality post-World Cup moderation, and Construction).

questions.title: Which country's mainland coastline will be confirmed contaminated by the Caroline Bezengi oil spill by August 13, 2026?
questions.background: The Caroline Bezengi has been leaking crude oil since running aground in June 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by government environmental authorities, or reliable news reports directly citing those statements. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the country whose mainland coastline is confirmed to have been contaminated by oil from the Caroline Bezengi by August 13, 2026. Offshore pollution, contamination confined to islands, and predictions of future landfall do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: June 11, 2026 reporting confirms the Cameroonian-flagged shadow-fleet crude tanker Caroline Bezengi struck a magnetic mine at the exit from the Gulf of Aden while bound for Sikka, India, and was moving slowly off the coast of Yemen before subsequently running aground in June. The resolution clause excluding island-only contamination points strongly to a grounding near Socotra (Yemen) or offshore Yemeni/Omani islands (such as Al Hallaniyat or Masirah). Because June-August is peak Southwest Monsoon with strong SW-to-NE winds and East Arabian surface currents pushing oil northeastward across the Arabian Sea, Yemen (closest mainland shore to the Gulf of Aden exit and Socotra) and Oman (directly downwind/downcurrent along Dhofar and Al Wusta) dominate, followed by Somalia and tail risk to India and Djibouti.

questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: June 29-July 1 reporting reshapes the Hormuz mine-clearance landscape: after French President Macron met Oman's Sultan Haitham in Paris on June 29 and announced France and Oman would work jointly with partners on demining, Iran angrily rejected foreign/European involvement on June 29-30 (Deputy FM Gharibabadi warning France against 'provocations'; FM spokesman Baqaei insisting demining under Article 5 of the Islamabad MoU is exclusively Iran's responsibility), and German Defense Minister Pistorius conceded July 1 that Germany does not expect to participate given Iran's refusal to cooperate with European countries. Meanwhile, US-Iran indirect technical talks on Hormuz shipping concluded July 1 in Doha mediated specifically by Qatar and Pakistan, and CBS News reiterated that Iran and Oman issued a bilateral joint statement last week on strait management. Oman's Paris demining alignment with France trims Oman modestly (0.29 -> 0.26, though Tehran aimed its public rebuke at France and Oman remains the sole co-littoral partner), while Tehran's hardened rejection of Western/G7 offers shifts mass toward non-Western partners capable of bilateral cooperation—China (0.23 -> 0.25), Islamabad MoU host and Doha mediator Pakistan (0.16 -> 0.18), and Russia (0.13 -> 0.14)—and trims Japan (0.04 -> 0.03), leaving 14% tail mass (Qatar, India, Turkey, UAE, US, etc.).

The strait, the narrow mouth of the Persian Gulf, has emerged as one of the top issues in negotiations to reach a permanent end to the Iran war. It wasn’t immediately clear what sparked the threat from Iran. local_articles.snippet: A ship ran aground in the Strait of Hormuz while using a route not approved by Iran, state television in Tehran reported Wednesday. The vessel was identified as a foreign container ship, with no other details. {{^htLoading}} {{/htLoading}} The report appeared aimed at underlining Tehran's claims to control the strait, which the world has long considered an international waterway. A fifth of all oil and natural gas passed through it in peacetime. Since the US and Israel launched the war against Iran on Feb 28, Iran has used its ability to choke off the waterway as a key source of leverage, disrupting global markets for energy and other critical goods. The strikes led to the start of the US-Iran war, which remains ongoing. From Pakistan, which is the mediating country between the US and Iran, to various political leaders in India, many foreign leaders are expected to fly out to Iran for the funeral procession. Who is on the list?
